newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt has 30 days to appeal Telebras ruling.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt has 30 days to appeal Telebras ruling.

text.p: The Brazilian government has 30 days to appeal a court ruling that allows a 1990 public share offering by federal telecoms giant Telebras, a company spokesman said.
A regional federal court formalized the ruling, issued in October, by publishing the decision in an official gazette Thursday, a court spokeswoman said.
The court backed a Telebras' 13.7-billion share subscription, rejecting a government appeal lodged in 1992 to block the issue based on allegations that the share price was undervalued.
The government, the main shareholder in Telebras, opposed the subscription on grounds it would hurt the company as it would dilute the value of existing shares.
With the publication of the ruling, the government may now appeal the decision to the Supreme Court, the Telebras spokesman said.
But the appeal is likely to reach the court only in February due to the Christmas and New Year's court recesses, so a final decision is expected to take months, he said.
The court ruling, which was made public in October, did not affect shares when it was published Thursday.
